title: Use of a High-throughput In Vitro Microfluidic System to Develop Oral Multi-species Biofilms
protocol: Recruit more than five individuals for saliva donation.
Ensure that no identifying information is taken from donors.
Exclude individuals who are ill, have taken oral antibiotics in the past three months, or have consumed food or liquid other than water in the previous two hours before donation.
Collect saliva in 50 ml plastic tubes.
Pool collected saliva in a plastic beaker and keep it on ice.
Do not use glass containers to avoid polymer adhesion from saliva.
Add DTT to the pooled saliva to achieve a final concentration of 2.5 mM from a 100x stock solution.
Stir the mixture for 10 minutes in a plastic beaker kept on ice.
Recruit more than five individuals for saliva donation.
Collect saliva in 50 ml plastic tubes at room temperature and pool the collected samples in a plastic beaker at room temperature.
Centrifuge pooled saliva for 30 min at 17,500 x g to remove particulate matter.
Dilute centrifuged saliva with three volumes of distilled water to achieve one-fourth concentration.
Filter-sterilize diluted saliva using a 0.22 μm polyethersulfone filter with low protein binding.
Freeze the pooled saliva at -80°C in individual use 50 ml plastic tubes containing no more than 35 ml.
Thaw frozen saliva at room temperature when needed for use.
Filter-sterilize thawed saliva again using a 0.22 μm polyethersulfone filter with low protein binding to remove precipitates.
Dilute pooled saliva with autoclaved general reagent grade glycerol to yield a stock with a final ratio of 25% glycerol, 75% cell-containing saliva [CCS].
Freeze diluted saliva at –80°C in 3 ml single-use aliquots until needed.
Thaw frozen saliva aliquot at room temperature.
Agitate thawed saliva gently on a vortexer for 5 sec.
Pipette thawed and agitated saliva into the microfluidic system as described in step 3 of the protocol.
Coat Bioflux microfluidic channels with CFS.
Add 100 µl of CFS to each outlet well.
Select “manual” using the Bioflux control software and set flow from channels “B1-B24” that are to be used.
Set shear to 1.0 dyne/cm² and start flow for 2 min at room temperature to ensure homogenous distribution of the CFS throughout the channel.
Ensure there is fluid in each inlet channel to verify that CFS flowed through all channels evenly.
Incubate plate at room temperature for 20 min.
Remove the CFS/pretreat solution from outlet wells and transfer to the inlet wells.
Add 100 μl of CCS inoculum to each outlet well.
Place the microfluidic plate on the heat plate set at 37 °C.
Select manual within the control software and set flow from outlet wells to inlet wells at 1.0 dyne/cm² for exactly 6 seconds.
Incubate the microfluidic plate at 37 °C for 40 minutes.
Aspirate waste inoculum from each of the outlet wells.
Add up to 1 ml total volume of CFS into each of the inlet wells.
Incubate the microfluidic plate at 37 °C, set program to run at 0.2 dyne/cm² for 20 hours.
Aspirate all fluid from the inlet and outlet wells.
Add 100 μl of PBS (pH 7.4) to each of the inlet wells.
Flow for 20 minutes at 0.2 dyne/cm².
Make 100 μl of stain mixture for each channel to be stained using SYTO 9 and propidium iodide according to commercial cell viability staining kit instructions.
Aspirate remaining PBS from the inlet wells.
Add 100 μl of the cell viability stain mixture to each inlet well.
Set to flow at 0.2 dyne/cm² and run solution from inlet to outlet for 45 minutes at room temperature.
Post-staining wash
Aspirate the remaining stain from each inlet well.
Add 100 µl of PBS to each inlet well.
Set the flow rate at 0.2 dyne/cm².
Run PBS solution from inlet to outlet for 20 min at room temperature.
Use an inverted confocal laser scanning microscope (CLSM) to collect biofilm image data from the microfluidic system.
Fit CLSM with a 40X 1.25 NA objective lens or similar quality lens.
Standardize emission capture gates with constant gain and offset measurements.
Ensure that laser power does not exceed 25%.
Convert CLSM files from Leica Image File type (LIF) to OME file type.
Use commercially available software such as IMARIS for conversion.
Render images in 3D using commercially available software such as IMARIS.
Perform 3D rendering using a combination of “Easy3D” and “Surpass” options.
Analyze the red channel using the “histogram” function of IMAGEJ.
Analyze the green channel using the “histogram” function of IMAGEJ.
Export data into a spreadsheet program.
Standardize all signal values by weighting each pixel.
Multiply the total count at a given signal intensity by its numerical value.
Sum all weighted values for both channels for each biofilm image.
Determine the percent total signal from either channel.
Calculate the relative ratio or percent red and percent green signal.
Perform statistical analyses, such as using two-tailed Student's T-test modified for unequal variance.
Harvest spent and unused saliva from inlet and outlet wells.
Wash the wells with 1 ml sterile distilled water three times.
Add 100 µl of sterile distilled water to the inlet wells.
Pass the sterile distilled water forward through the channels at >8.0 dyne/cm2 for at least 5 min.
Pass the sterile distilled water in reverse direction for at least 5 min.
Repeat the forward and reverse washing steps.
Check by light or epifluorescence microscopy for thorough biofilm removal.
Collect the 100 µl cell-suspension.
Store the collected cell-suspension at -80°C for culture-independent analysis.
